# Part 1: Template Map (6-page limit)

**Rule of thumb:** 11pt single-spaced text runs about 550-600 words per page. Headings, tables, and spacing eat room, so I've targeted about 5.5 pages of text, leaving a buffer. Check the funder's margin and font rules.

| Narrative Subsection | Page Limit | Target Words | Rubric Criteria | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need | 1.5 | ~750 | Need/Community Impact (problem, population, data) | 30% |
| Program Design & Activities | 2.0 | ~950 | Program Design (logic, activities); track-record sentences for Org Capacity | 30% (+ part of 5%) |
| Outcomes & Evaluation | 1.0 | ~525 | Outcomes & Evaluation (measurable outcomes, methods, baseline) | 20% |
| Staffing & Implementation Timeline | 0.5 | ~250 (mostly a table) | Program Design (staffing, timeline) | within 30% |
| Budget & Cost Effectiveness | 1.0 | ~525 | Budget & Cost Effectiveness; sustainability paragraph | 15% (+ part of 5%) |
| **Total** | **6.0** | **~3,000** | | |

**Gap to plan for:** The template has no Organizational Capacity & Sustainability section, but the rubric scores it at 5%. Cover it this way:
- **Capacity:** 2-3 sentences of track record in Need and in the close of Program Design (included in the drafts below), plus attachments (financials, résumés, letters).
- **Sustainability:** a ~100-word paragraph at the end of the Budget narrative.

**Attachment use (10 max):** budget form, logic model, timeline/Gantt, 2-3 letters, key résumés, financials/audit, evaluation instrument or data-sharing agreement. Reference each by name in the narrative, e.g., "(see Attachment 2: Logic Model)".

---

# Part 2: Draft, Need (~750 words)

Bracketed items are information I don't have. Please fill them in or confirm them, and don't submit with brackets in place.

---

## Need

**Low adult literacy is a widespread, measurable barrier in Riverbend.** In a city of 45,000, roughly one in four adults (24%) has low literacy (ACS 2020). That is approximately [X] residents, based on an adult population of [X], who may struggle to complete a job application, read a medication label, or help a child with homework. Low literacy is closely tied to lower earnings, higher unemployment, and poorer health outcomes [cite 1-2 sources; add a local figure if available, such as the unemployment rate or median income for adults without a high school credential]. For Riverbend families, this is an everyday barrier to economic stability.

**Demand for services exceeds local capacity.** In 2024, local libraries reported a combined waitlist of 120 adults seeking ESL and literacy services. That waitlist alone equals nearly 40% of the 310 adults our program served last year. [Insert: our own waitlist or turn-away numbers, typical wait time, and whether our classes were at capacity.] Adults who cannot access instruction when they are motivated often do not return, and the need compounds over time.

**The problem is intergenerational.** The county school district reports 1,200 K-12 students reading below grade level (2023). Parents' literacy is among the strongest predictors of children's reading success [cite]. Strengthening adult literacy in Riverbend therefore supports the next generation's reading outcomes as well as the adults themselves. [If applicable: note how many of our learners are parents of school-age children.]

**Who we will serve.** This project will serve adults 18 and older who live in Riverbend [and surrounding county communities] and read below [the 8th-grade level / NRS Educational Functioning Level X]. We prioritize [e.g., parents of school-age children, job seekers, adults without a high school credential, English language learners]. [Add the demographic profile of current learners: age range, income, race/ethnicity or language background, employment status.] These adults are underserved because [barriers, e.g., limited daytime availability, transportation, childcare, cost, stigma, or lack of nearby classes].

**What our experience shows.** In 2024, we served 310 adults. Of these, 40% (about 124) achieved at least one level of gain on a standardized reading assessment ([name of assessment], 2024 internal evaluation). This result establishes three things:

- Adults in Riverbend can make measurable progress with the right instruction.
- We have a documented baseline against which to measure improvement.
- There is clear room to do better: [60% did not show a level gain, due to (e.g., attendance gaps, insufficient instructional hours, or learners leaving before post-testing)].

This proposal is built to close that gap by [raising the level-gain rate from 40% to X%] while expanding access for waitlisted adults.

**Why now.** [One or two sentences on timeliness, e.g., a local employer or workforce initiative that requires literacy credentials, a loss of other funding, rising ESL enrollment, or new district partnerships.] Without added capacity, the adults on Riverbend's waitlists will continue to wait, and their children will continue to enter classrooms in homes where reading support is limited.

---

**Notes on the Need draft**
1. **Verify the "24% low literacy (ACS 2020)" attribution.** The American Community Survey doesn't directly measure literacy. Figures like this usually come from NCES/PIAAC model-based estimates or from ACS proxies such as educational attainment or English proficiency. A reviewer who knows this may question the citation, so confirm the source and wording.
2. **Check the 120 waitlist figure.** It's described as "ESL/waitlist," so make sure it represents adults who need literacy services, not only English-language learners, and that it doesn't duplicate people on your own list.
3. **Confirm the denominator for the 40% gain.** If it's 40% of those who were post-tested rather than of all 310, say so. Reviewers will notice, and the honest framing is more credible.

---

# Part 3: Draft, Program Design & Activities (~950 words)

I don't know your actual program model, so the specific activities, hours, and ratios are placeholders to confirm. Edit them to match what you do or plan to do.

---

## Program Design & Activities

**Overview.** [Program Name] will provide [X hours/week] of structured reading instruction and supports to [N] Riverbend adults per year, with the goal of increasing the share who achieve a measurable reading gain from 40% to [X]%. Each element of the design responds to a gap identified in our Need statement. We will add cohorts to reduce waitlists, concentrate instruction on learners' own goals to improve persistence, and track progress to confirm that learners are actually advancing. (See Attachment [#]: Logic Model.)

**Core activities**

1. **Intake and assessment.** Every learner completes a standardized reading assessment ([name]) and a goals interview within [two weeks] of enrolling. Results set the starting level, establish the baseline for evaluation, and shape an individual learning plan. *Addresses: the need for measurable baselines and appropriate placement.*

2. **Small-group reading instruction.** Learners attend [X sessions per week, X hours each, for X weeks] in groups of no more than [X], led by [trained instructors/volunteer tutors supervised by instructors] at [location(s), including times such as evenings]. Instruction is explicit and sequenced, covering the core components of reading (word recognition, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension) using materials tied to learners' goals, such as workplace documents, health forms, and children's school materials. *Addresses: low reading levels and the low 40% gain rate by increasing instructional intensity.*

3. **[One-to-one tutoring / digital practice].** Learners who need extra support receive [X hours/week] of tutoring or self-paced practice using [tool]. [CONFIRM or DELETE.] *Addresses: variation in learner starting points and schedule barriers.*

4. **Persistence supports.** Staff contact learners after [one missed session], help resolve barriers such as [transportation vouchers, childcare, schedule changes], and hold progress conferences every [X weeks]. [CONFIRM or DELETE.] *Addresses: attrition, a common reason adults do not reach a measurable gain.*

5. **[Family literacy component, optional].** [Parents receive X sessions on reading with children, with books provided.] *Addresses: the intergenerational link to the 1,200 K-12 students reading below grade level.* [DELETE if not part of the program.]

6. **Transition and follow-up.** At exit, learners receive a post-assessment and a next-step plan (e.g., [GED/HSE preparation, ESL, job training, library programs]). We follow up at [3 and 6 months] to document outcomes.

**Participant pathway**

| Stage | Timing | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Outreach & referral | Ongoing | Referrals from libraries, schools, [employers, social service partners]; waitlisted adults contacted first |
| 2. Intake & assessment | Weeks 0-2 | Baseline assessment, goals interview, learning plan |
| 3. Instruction | Weeks 2-[X] | [X hours/week] of group instruction plus [tutoring/practice] |
| 4. Progress check | Every [X] weeks | Attendance review, check-in, plan adjustment |
| 5. Post-assessment | At [X hours] or week [X] | Re-test; level gain recorded |
| 6. Transition & follow-up | Exit, then 3 and 6 months | Next-step referral; outcome check |

**Evidence base.** Our approach draws on research-based principles for adult reading instruction, which emphasize explicit instruction in the components of reading, sufficient instructional time, and content connected to adult learners' real-life goals [cite, e.g., Kruidenier, 2002; U.S. Department of Education LINCS resources; verify before citing]. Research on adult learner persistence shows that adults are more likely to stay and progress when programs address practical barriers and set clear, personal goals [cite, e.g., Comings et al., NCSALL; verify before citing]. We apply these principles through goal-linked materials, structured group instruction, and proactive persistence supports. Our own results provide local evidence: 40% of the 310 learners we served in 2024 achieved a level gain, and we have used what we learned, [specific lesson, e.g., "that learners with fewer than X hours rarely advance"], to redesign [dosage/schedule/supports] for this project.

**Why we can deliver.** [Organization] has operated since [year] and served [number] adults, with [financial/partnership strengths, e.g., clean audits, existing partnerships with the library and school district]. The staff and implementation plan (next section) and the letters of support in Attachment [#] show readiness to start within [X] weeks of award.

---

**What I need from you to finalize Program Design**
- Actual instructional model, hours per week, class size, and program length
- Which of activities 3, 4, and 5 are real (delete the rest)
- Assessment tool name
- Venue(s) and schedule
- Number of learners to be served under this grant
- The lesson learned from the 40% result, and what has changed
- Partner names for referrals

**Verify these before citing:** Kruidenier (2002) and the Comings/NCSALL persistence work are sources I'd expect to fit, but confirm the exact citations and claims yourself. I haven't inserted statistics I can't verify.

Once you send those details, I can tighten both drafts to exact page counts and move on to Outcomes & Evaluation, Staffing/Timeline, and Budget.

# Rubric-First Outline: Where Each Criterion Gets Scored

The earlier map went from template to rubric. This one goes from rubric to template, so you can check that every scoring element is covered and see where the evidence lives.

## 1. Overview crosswalk

| Rubric Criterion | Weight | Primary Location | Supporting Locations | Narrative Space |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need/Community Impact | 30% | Need (1.5 pp) | Program Design opening; Attachments (data sources, letters) | ~25% of pages |
| Program Design & Activities | 30% | Program Design (2 pp) + Staffing/Timeline (0.5 pp) | Logic model, Gantt, résumés | ~42% of pages |
| Outcomes & Evaluation | 20% | Outcomes & Evaluation (1 pp) | Need (baseline), logic model, evaluation instrument | ~17% of pages |
| Budget & Cost Effectiveness | 15% | Budget narrative (1 pp) | Budget form attachment | ~17% of pages |
| Org Capacity & Sustainability | 5% | No dedicated section | Track-record sentences in Need and Program Design; sustainability paragraph in Budget; financials, letters, résumés | ~3% of pages |

**Space check:** Outcomes & Evaluation gets 17% of the pages for 20% of the score. Since the funder's page maxima total exactly 6, you can't expand it. Tighten Need and Program Design prose slightly, and use a table for outcomes so the page works harder.

## 2. Criterion-by-criterion outline

### A. Need/Community Impact (30%)
Scored on: clarity of problem, target population, data.

| Scoring element | Where | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Problem clearly stated | Need, opening paragraph | 24% low literacy, with the source verified | Drafted; **verify ACS attribution** |
| Local quantified data | Need | School district (1,200), library waitlist (120), your 310 served | Drafted |
| Target population defined | Need, "Who we will serve" | Eligibility, demographics, barriers | **Needs your demographic data** |
| Gap in services | Need | Waitlist vs. capacity, your own turn-aways | **Needs your waitlist/turn-away numbers** |
| Why now | Need, closing paragraph | A local trigger | **Needs your input** |

**Hook:** "Demand exceeds capacity: [120] adults are waitlisted at local libraries alone, equal to [X]% of everyone we served last year."

### B. Program Design & Activities (30%)
Scored on: logic, timeline, staffing.

| Scoring element | Where | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Logic (need → activity → outcome) | Program Design; Attachment: Logic Model | Each activity tagged with the need it addresses | Drafted; **logic model to build** |
| Evidence base | Program Design | Research citations plus your own 40% result | **Verify citations** |
| Participant pathway | Program Design table | Intake through follow-up | Drafted; needs real hours and dates |
| Timeline | Staffing & Timeline section; Attachment: Gantt | Quarterly milestones, start-up steps | Not yet drafted |
| Staffing | Staffing & Timeline section; résumés | Role, FTE, qualifications, ratio | Not yet drafted |

**Hook:** "Each element responds to a gap in the Need section: [activity] addresses [barrier] by [mechanism]."

### C. Outcomes & Evaluation (20%)
Scored on: measurable outcomes, methods, baseline.

| Scoring element | Where | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measurable outcomes | Outcomes table | 2-4 SMART objectives | Not yet drafted |
| Baseline | Outcomes; echo in Need | **40% level gain (2024)**, with the denominator clarified | Data in hand; confirm denominator |
| Methods | Evaluation paragraph | Pre/post standardized assessment, attendance data, follow-up at 3 and 6 months | Not yet drafted |
| Use of results | Evaluation paragraph | Quarterly review and program adjustments | Not yet drafted |

**Suggested structure (one page):** a table of outcomes (outcome / baseline / target / measure / timing) at about 40% of the page, then short paragraphs on method, data ownership, and improvement. Draft targets, which you must set realistically:
- Learners achieving one-level gain: 40% → [X]%
- Learners served per year: 310 → [X]
- Waitlisted adults enrolled: [X]
- Average instructional hours completed: [baseline] → [target]

**Hook:** "By [date], [X]% of participants will achieve at least one level of gain, up from a 2024 baseline of 40% (n=310), measured by [assessment]."

### D. Budget & Cost Effectiveness (15%)
Scored on: clear budget, justification.

| Scoring element | Where | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Clear budget | Attachment: budget form | Line items match staffing and activities |
| Justification | Budget narrative | Rationale per major category |
| Cost effectiveness | Budget narrative | Cost per participant and per level gain; comparison benchmark |
| Leverage | Budget narrative | In-kind, match, partner contributions |

**Hook:** "At $[X] per learner and $[Y] per level gain, this project [compares to benchmark]."
**Consistency check:** FTEs in the staffing table, the budget form, and the narrative must all agree.

### E. Org Capacity & Sustainability (5%)
No dedicated section, so seed it in three places:
1. **Need:** one sentence on the 310 served and 40% gain.
2. **Program Design close:** years operating, partnerships, readiness to launch.
3. **Budget narrative close (~100 words):** funding diversification, committed support, and a plan to continue after the grant.

Attachments carry the rest: financials/audit, letters of support, résumés.

## 3. Attachment plan (10 max)

| # | Attachment | Criteria served |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Budget form | Budget |
| 2 | Logic model | Program Design, Outcomes |
| 3 | Timeline/Gantt | Program Design |
| 4-5 | Letters of support/MOUs (library, school district) | Need, Capacity |
| 6 | Key staff résumés | Program Design, Capacity |
| 7 | Financials/audit | Capacity, Budget |
| 8 | Assessment tool/evaluation plan or data-sharing agreement | Outcomes |
| 9 | Data source summary (ACS, district, library) | Need |
| 10 | Reserve (e.g., board list, org chart, waitlist documentation) | Capacity |

## 4. Cross-section consistency (reviewers check this)

- The **40% baseline** appears the same way in Need, Program Design, and Outcomes.
- **Participant numbers** match in Program Design, Outcomes, and Budget (cost per participant).
- Every **activity** maps to a stated need and a measured outcome.
- **Staffing** matches across the staffing table, budget form, and résumés.
- Use the **funder's rubric terms** as headings or bolded lead-ins so reviewers can find the scoring elements quickly.

## 5. Self-scoring checklist before submission

For each criterion, ask whether a reviewer could find the answer in under 30 seconds:
- **Need:** Is the problem quantified locally, with a cited source and year?
- **Design:** Can a reader trace one activity from need to outcome?
- **Outcomes:** Is there a baseline, a target, and a measurement tool for every outcome?
- **Budget:** Is cost per participant stated and justified?
- **Capacity:** Are track record, financials, and sustainability each visible somewhere?

## Next steps

The sections still undrafted are **Outcomes & Evaluation**, **Staffing & Timeline**, and **Budget**. If you send me your target number of learners, the level-gain target you're comfortable promising, the assessment tool name, and your rough budget total, I can draft Outcomes & Evaluation next. That section is where your 40% baseline turns into points.

# Outcomes & Evaluation (draft, ~1 page)

Bracketed items need your input. Please resolve them before submitting.

---

## Outcomes & Evaluation

Our evaluation asks whether more Riverbend adults gain measurable reading skills than before, and whether those gains hold. We will track four SMART objectives against a documented 2024 baseline. (See Attachment [#]: Logic Model and Attachment [#]: Evaluation Plan.)

| Outcome | Baseline | Target | Measure | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Reading gain:** learners advancing at least one level | 40% (124 of 310, 2024) | **55%** by month 12, maintained each year after | TABE Reading, pre/post | Pre at intake; post at exit or after [X] instructional hours |
| **2. Reach:** adults enrolled per year | 310 (2024) | **420 per year**, including at least [X] waitlisted adults | Enrollment records | Quarterly |
| **3. Post-test completion:** enrollees with valid pre/post pairs | [X]% (2024) | **At least [80]%** of enrollees | Data system | Quarterly |
| **4. Sustained progress:** exiters reached and showing retained level or a next step (HSE, ESL, training, employment) | Not previously collected; set in Year 1 | **At least [X]%** of exiters reached; [X]% retaining level or in a next step | Phone/text follow-up | 3 and 6 months after exit |

**Baseline and design.** Our baseline is the 2024 result: 124 of 310 learners (40%) gained at least one level on TABE Reading. We will calculate the gain rate the same way each year, as learners with valid pre- and post-tests who advanced at least one level divided by all learners with valid test pairs. We will also report gain as a share of all enrollees, so reviewers can see the effect of attrition. We will use a pre/post design with the same instrument and alternate forms, with post-testing timed to publisher guidelines for minimum instructional hours. This design shows change in participants but cannot prove that instruction caused it. To strengthen the evidence, we will, if consent and capacity allow, pre-test adults on partner waitlists and retest them at comparable intervals as a matched comparison. Otherwise, we will compare results with our 2024 cohort and report the comparison as descriptive.

**Data, privacy, and improvement.** The Program Manager will collect intake, attendance, and post-test data in [data system] and run monthly completeness checks. A contracted evaluator, [name or "an external M&E consultant"], will analyze gain, attendance, and completion quarterly by class, site, and learner subgroup. Learners consent to data use at intake. Records are stored in a password-protected, access-restricted system, and only de-identified aggregate results are reported externally [add applicable requirements, e.g., FERPA or state rules]. Findings drive action. Staff, instructors, and partners will review quarterly results, and any class falling below [X]% gain or [X]% attendance triggers a response within 30 days, such as schedule changes, added tutoring, or intensified persistence outreach. We will share annual results with the funder and partners and use them to refine the next year's design.

---

## Check these before dropping it in

1. **Baseline denominator.** Earlier you said 310 adults were *served*. Now 124 of 310 were *post-tested*. Both are true only if every learner was post-tested, which is unusual, and reviewers may question it. If some of the 310 weren't tested, the 40% is a share of all served, and the wording should say "124 of 310 enrolled learners." Also fill in the 2024 post-test completion rate for Objective 3.
2. **"Maintain 420."** Your 2024 baseline is 310, so 420 is a 35% expansion. I wrote "420 per year" with 310 as the baseline. Make sure Program Design and Budget say the same, and explain how you'll add capacity.
3. **The jump to 55% is large.** At 420 learners, 55% means about 231 gains versus 124 now, an increase of roughly 86%. Reviewers will look for the reason. Program Design should connect it to specific changes such as more hours, persistence supports, and the lesson from the 2024 results.
4. **Cost math.** $150,000 ÷ 420 ≈ $357 per participant holds only if the $150,000 is annual. If it's a multi-year total, restate it per year. If all 420 are post-tested at 55%, cost per level gain is about $649, a useful number for the Budget section.
5. **"55% year-end."** I read this as month 12 of the grant. Confirm, and say whether the rate must hold in later years.
6. **Fit.** This runs roughly 520 words with the table. If it spills over a page, shorten the comparison-group sentence first, then the privacy detail, since the table carries the scoring elements.
7. **Fill in:** post-test hours threshold, Objective 3 baseline, Objective 4 targets, data system, evaluator name, and privacy requirements.

If you send the answers to items 1 through 4, I'll reconcile the numbers across all sections. Staffing & Timeline is next, then Budget.

Since then you've added real numbers and a drafted Outcomes section, so here is an updated version showing where each criterion stands and what's still exposed. If you wanted a different angle, such as a reviewer-style scoring sheet or a one-page checklist, tell me and I'll switch.

# Updated Rubric Outline (status as of now)

| Criterion | Weight | Where scored | Pages | Status | Biggest risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need/Community Impact | 30% | Need | 1.5 | Drafted, with gaps | Unverified ACS "24% low literacy" source; no demographics, turn-away numbers, or "why now" yet |
| Program Design & Activities | 30% | Program Design + Staffing/Timeline | 2.0 + 0.5 | Design drafted with placeholders; **Staffing/Timeline not drafted** | Must justify 310 → 420 learners and 40% → 55% gain with concrete changes |
| Outcomes & Evaluation | 20% | Outcomes & Evaluation | 1.0 | Drafted | Baseline denominator and several blanks to fill |
| Budget & Cost Effectiveness | 15% | Budget narrative + budget form | 1.0 | **Not drafted** | Cost figures must match everywhere; no benchmark yet |
| Org Capacity & Sustainability | 5% | No dedicated section | Spread across sections | Partly seeded | Sustainability paragraph not yet written |

## Where the points are most at risk

1. **Program Design (30%) is the largest exposure.** The draft is full of placeholders. A reviewer will ask why the program can grow 35% and raise the gain rate by 15 points. The design needs a stated answer, such as more instructional hours, persistence supports, added cohorts, or added staff.
2. **Need (30%) is solid on structure but thin on proof.** Fixing the ACS attribution and adding your own waitlist and demographic data would move it the most.
3. **Budget (15%) is a blank.** It's only 15%, but unwritten sections score zero, and it ties your numbers together.

## Number ledger (must match everywhere)

| Figure | Value | Appears in | Open question |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 served | 310 | Need, Program Design, Outcomes | Were all 310 post-tested? |
| 2024 gain | 40% (124/310) | Need, Program Design, Outcomes | Denominator: enrolled or post-tested? |
| Target served | 420/year | Program Design, Outcomes, Budget | Per year or total? How is capacity added? |
| Target gain | 55% | Program Design, Outcomes | Of valid test pairs or all enrolled? |
| Request | $150,000 | Budget, Cover Page | Annual or multi-year? |
| Cost/participant | ≈ $357 | Budget, Executive items | Holds only if $150,000 is annual |
| Cost/level gain | ≈ $649 (at 231 gains) | Budget | Only if all 420 are post-tested; recompute for your real completion rate |

## Criterion-to-section checklist

- **Need:** quantified local problem, defined population, service gap, "why now." Needs your waitlist, demographics, and trigger.
- **Program Design:** each activity tagged to a need and an outcome, evidence base, pathway, and staffing and timeline. Needs the real model (hours, class size, venue), staffing table, and quarterly milestones.
- **Outcomes:** SMART objectives, baseline, methods, and use of results. Mostly done. Fill in the post-test hours, Objective 3 baseline, Objective 4 targets, data system, and evaluator.
- **Budget:** clear budget, justification, cost per participant and per gain, leverage. Needs line items and a benchmark.
- **Capacity/Sustainability:** track record in Need and Program Design, plus a ~100-word sustainability paragraph at the end of Budget. Needs funding sources and commitments.

## Suggested order from here

1. Draft **Staffing & Timeline** (0.5 page, mostly a table). It defines how you reach 420 learners and also feeds the budget.
2. Draft **Budget & Cost Effectiveness**, including the sustainability paragraph.
3. Resolve the number ledger above, then reconcile all five sections.
4. Do a final fit check against the 6-page limit and a rubric self-score.

To start on Staffing & Timeline, I need the roles and FTEs you plan to fund (and any existing staff), the grant start date and period, and how you'll add capacity for the extra 110 learners (more classes, sites, tutors, or hours).

# Reviewer Scoring Sheet (100 points)

## 1. Need/Community Impact (30 pts)
